title: Coverage-Guided Fuzzer Loop
description: An animated simulation of how a coverage-guided fuzzer explores a target program's basic blocks over time, reaching the deep bug block far faster than pure random fuzzing.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

educational.topic: Software Assurance and Supply Chain Security
learningObjectives: Describe the coverage-guided fuzzing loop: mutate, execute, keep inputs that reach new code.
Compare the exploration behavior of coverage-guided versus random fuzzing.
Explain why coverage guidance dramatically reduces time-to-bug for deep code paths.
educational.prerequisites: Basic understanding of control flow, branches, and software testing.

pedagogical.interaction: Mutation-aggressiveness and inputs-per-second sliders, a Coverage-guided toggle for A/B comparison, and a Reset button.
pedagogical.assessment: Lesson plan asks students to run both modes and compare time-to-crash.
pedagogical.misconceptions: Counters the idea that random fuzzing is as effective as coverage-guided fuzzing for deep bugs.
